meta.source: Greyscale Workbooklet.dotm, as captured in the greyscale-print-design-system skill

tokens.name: ink
tokens.usage: Body text and all headings on `reverse` (21:1), `pale` (12.9:1), `accent-1` (7.2:1) and `accent-2` (5.8:1). Never on `accent-4`–`accent-6` (3.0–1.8:1).

tokens.name: accent-1
tokens.usage: Lightest table shading. Text on it: `ink` (7.2:1). Not `reverse` (2.9:1). Not in the coding set — too close to its neighbours to mark a category; use for decoration and fills.

tokens.name: accent-2
tokens.usage: Light table shading. Text on it: `ink` (5.8:1). Not `reverse` (3.6:1). Part of the coding set (pale / accent-2 / accent-4 / accent-6): the only four shades used to tell categories apart.

tokens.name: accent-3
tokens.usage: Mid shading — the tipping point: `ink` 4.67:1 and `reverse` 4.50:1, both at the edge. Printer tone gain can push either below 4.5:1, so use it for fills, bars and rules without text, or with bold text 14pt+ only. Not in the coding set — too close to its neighbours to mark a category; use for decoration and fills.

tokens.name: accent-4
tokens.usage: Dark shading for header rows and example-response panels. Text on it: `reverse` (7.0:1). Never `ink` (3.0:1). Part of the coding set (pale / accent-2 / accent-4 / accent-6): the only four shades used to tell categories apart.

tokens.name: accent-5
tokens.usage: Dark shading. Text on it: `reverse` (8.9:1). Never `ink` (2.4:1). Not in the coding set — too close to its neighbours to mark a category; use for decoration and fills.

tokens.name: accent-6
tokens.usage: Darkest table shading. Text on it: `reverse` (11.6:1). Never `ink` (1.8:1). Part of the coding set (pale / accent-2 / accent-4 / accent-6): the only four shades used to tell categories apart.

tokens.name: muted
tokens.usage: Caption, Subtle and Intense Reference on `reverse` (6.5:1). On `pale` it drops to 4.0:1 — use `ink` for captions on pale panels.

tokens.name: link
tokens.usage: Hyperlink — changed 29 Sept 2026 from #898A89 (3.5:1, too faint) to the Muted grey: 6.5:1 on paper. Always underline links; on `pale` use `ink` underlined (link is 4.0:1 there). Update the Hyperlink style in Greyscale Workbooklet.dotm to match.

tokens.name: pale
tokens.usage: Block Text panels and grid module fills. Text on it: `ink` (12.9:1). Not `reverse` (1.6:1) or `link` (2.1:1). Part of the coding set (pale / accent-2 / accent-4 / accent-6): the only four shades used to tell categories apart.

tokens.name: reverse
tokens.usage: The paper, and text on `accent-4`–`accent-6` fills only (7.0–11.6:1) — Example Response and White Table Heading styles. Never on `accent-1`–`accent-3` or `pale`.

styles.name: h1
styles.usage: Heading 1 — Lato Black 52pt, centred, keep with next.

styles.name: normal
styles.usage: Normal — Lato 12pt, left; 3.5mm after, 4.9mm line spacing.

styles.name: mc-answers
styles.usage: `3. Multiple Choice Answers Format` — 6mm indent, 2.1mm before/after.

styles.name: writing-lines
styles.usage: `Writing Lines` / `5. Writing Lines` — 2mm indent, 6.35mm line; three lines ≈ one 20mm row module.

styles.name: white-table-heading
styles.usage: `White Table Heading (12pt)` — white, only on `accent-4`–`accent-6` fills.

tokens.name: margin-booklet-inside
tokens.usage: Saddle-stapled booklet: inside (spine). Word: leftMargin with Book fold on.

tokens.name: margin-booklet-outside
tokens.usage: Saddle-stapled booklet: outside. Proof it — some printers can't image within 10mm of the edge.

tokens.name: fold-clear-zone
tokens.usage: Keep text and rules this far either side of the booklet fold.

tokens.name: col-gutter
tokens.usage: Between columns; build as real spacer columns in Word tables.

tokens.name: rhythm-unit
tokens.usage: Row module + gutter; make space-before + line + space-after add up to it.
